title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 37
paragraphs: Thus he replied, and while the Mysians were content with this answer, Croesus’s son came in, having heard of the request made by the Mysians. When Croesus said he would not send his son with them, the young man spoke as follows: “Father, in former times the fairest and noblest lot was allotted to us: to go out continually to war and to the hunt, and so to gain good repute. But now you have barred me from both of these, even though you have never observed in me any cowardly or faint-hearted spirit. With what face must I now appear as I come to and from the market-place of the city? What kind of a man shall I be thought by the citizens, and what kind of a man shall I be thought by my newly-married wife? With what sort of husband will she think herself matched? Therefore either let me go to the hunt, or persuade me with reason that things are better for me as they now stand.”
